title: Quarterly Cadence Charter & Escalation Matrix for Hosted API + Model Fleet Sync
creator: Marina Chen
description: Establish a repeatable quarterly cadence and a lightweight escalation matrix to synchronize roadmap decisions, model onboarding windows, and canary schedules between the Hosted API surface and the model fleet used in production. This charter defines meeting rhythms, required artifacts for a model to enter the Hosted API catalog, decision owners for rollouts and rollbacks, and an escalation path for SLO/regression events that cross product/engineering boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A documented quarterly cadence (planning, freeze, canary, retrospective) published to Confluence
A one-page escalation matrix with named owners for Level 1/2/3 decisions and SLAs for acknowledgement and resolution
A checklist template that PMs and Model Ops use for model onboarding that gates Hosted API listing
Three simulated handoffs executed in March runbook drills with post-mortem notes and action items
tasks: Draft charter and circulate to Eng, Design, Model Ops, Security (owner: Diego)
Create model onboarding checklist and attach to Hosted API catalog repo (owner: Model Ops)
Schedule recurring alignment forum (30m bi-weekly) and invite stakeholders (owner: Diego)
Run two tabletop drills simulating a model-quality regression and cross-region capacity outage (owners: SRE + PM)
Publish final charter and route to execs for acknowledgement
decisions: Use a 6-week pre-commit window before any model is eligible for Hosted API listing
Canary cadence: 3-stage (internal prod -> limited tenant -> general) with 48h observation per stage
Model rollback decision authority: Eng Lead (first 48h) then Product Director if broader customer impact
SLO regression triggers require immediate escalation to on-call SRE and PM within 30 minutes
risks: If cadence introduces too much upfront gating, Hosted API velocity may slow and frustrate downstream teams
Ambiguity in ownership could slow rollbacks; must be mitigated by named owners and SLAs
Model Ops capacity to complete checklist tasks may be a bottleneck during a large onboarding quarter
next_steps: Incorporate feedback from Eng Leads by 2025-03-10
Finalize charter and checklist, then publish to Confluence (target 2025-03-14)
Run first tabletop drill during Cycle 2025-W13 and capture action items
Set up a lightweight dashboard in the Console to expose cadence-related metrics (canary success rate, time-to-list, rollback latency)
